EXCLUSIVE: 'I had an unforgettable night among the spirits at NYC's ghosts boos and booze haunted pub crawl'

To get into the Halloween spirit, I embarked on New York City's spookiest walking ghost tour and haunted pub crawl exploring the chilling past of the West Village

I had an unforgettable night among the spirits as I embarked on the haunting 'Ghosts Boos and Booze Haunted Pub Crawl,' exploring the eerie history of the West Village.

On September 29, I, along with a group of fellow horror lovers, was led by the talented tour guide Jonathan Gunning through a bone-chilling ghost tour, learning all about the eerie tales of New York City's past. As we wandered through the streets on a crisp fall night, we stopped at many places, including historic pubs, restaurants, homes, and public parks, learning about their mysterious histories.

From shooting back Fireball shots to getting goosebumps over the tales of spirits still lingering around us, this was hands down the perfect tour to get into the fall spirit. This comes as the Queen of Halloween, Heidi Klum, recently released her new limited-edition fall collaboration with Apothic wine.

There were many fascinating stops along the tour, starting off at the haunted grounds of the bar One if by Land, Two if by Sea, located at 17 Barrow Street in the West Village. While peeking into the establishment, we were told all about the scandalous story of Vice President Aaron Burr.

The lore surrounding the building claims that up to 20 ghosts live there, including Burr and his daughter, Theodosia. Customers and staff at the restaurant have reported floating objects, flickering lights, and unexplainable occurrences at the bar - including the legend that Theodosia playfully steals the earrings off women drinking.

Shortly after, we were guided to Washington Square Park, widely considered one of the most haunted locations in the Big Apple. Many believe that the park is filled with a haunted energy, as historians have confirmed that over 20,000 human bodies remain buried directly under the park's grass and plazas.

Between 1797 and 1825, this land was used as a potter's field for the poor, criminals, and victims of yellow fever. Over the years that followed, construction workers have claimed to have unearthed human bones and old gravestones.

Many park visitors have also claimed that they have witnessed paranormal activity in the space, including reports of a weeping woman, the sound of giggling phantom children, and unexplained cold spots.

In addition to sharing these facts beneath the Washington Square arches, the tour also included a stop at The Hangman's Elm, New York City's oldest surviving tree.

The landmark is known for being a spot for public executions, and is infamously known for the hanging of an enslaved woman named Rose Butler in 1819. This 19-year-old girl was hanged in the park for arson, and is known as the last person to ever be hanged in the square.

The tour went on to take us to several other historical sites, including The Brown Building, Down the Hatch, and a haunted residence on Gay Street. I highly recommend this tour for both locals and visitors if you're looking for an affordable and thrilling way to get into the Halloween spirit.
